editorial_contributions.text: The present article is a survey of results contained in the paper ``Colorings of metric spaces'' by \textit{M. Benda} and \textit{M. Perles} (written in 1976 and circulated in preprint form, but published only recently [Geombinatorics 9, No. 3, 113-126 (2000; Zbl 0951.05037)]), as well as some subsequent developments on open problems posed in it. Given a metric space \(X\) and a positive number \(r\), the graph \((X,r)\) has vertices the points of \(X\), with \(x\) and \(y\) joined by an edge iff the distance between \(x\) and \(y\) is \(r\). The problems discussed in the article are concerned primarily with determining the chromatic number and the connectivity of graphs of the form \((X,r)\). Specifically, (1) determine the chromatic number of \((Q^n,1)\) for \(n \geq 5\), and of \((X,1)\), when \(X\) is a finite algebraic extension of \(Q^2\), (2) characterize the subgroup of \(Q^n\) generated by the elements of length 1 (\((Q^n,1)\) is connected if and only if this group is all of \(Q^n\)), and similarly for \(F^n\), when \(F\) is a finite real algebraic extension of \(Q\) and (3) determine the connectivity of \((F^n,1)\), when \(F\) is either \(Q(\sqrt{n_1},\dots,\sqrt{n_t})\) with \(n_1,\dots,n_t \in Q\) or \(Q(\alpha)\), where \(\alpha\) is a real algebraic number.
